evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We work with 2,400 smallholder farmers in Chipata district, Zambia. Each gets a seed-and-fertilizer voucher card, fully paid, to redeem at any of three agro-dealers between 1 and 21 November. In our survey of 300 farmers 88% said they would redeem; dealer records show 54% did. In interviews, those who did not said they meant to go on a market day and the window closed; nobody mentioned cost or distrust, and stock records show no shortages. The dealers are in Chipata town, on the Katete road, and at Chiparamba, open Monday to Saturday, 8am to 5pm; the farmer brings the voucher card and a national registration card. Extension officers hand out the cards at village meetings in the last week of October and spend a few minutes with each farmer, in Chinyanja. Draft the plan prompt.
evals.expected_output: A plan prompt in the output template, written as an if-then sentence whose blanks take only the dates, hours, and dealers the user gave.
assertions: The prompt is an if-then sentence with blanks for a day, a time, and a place.
The real options listed are the user's: 1 to 21 November, Monday to Saturday, 8am to 5pm, three dealers.
Has the farmer say the plan back once, and says who else sees or hears the plan.
Specifies a pretest with the number of people and what counts as a pass.
Promises no effect size for this program.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Attendance at our vaccination camp is low. Add a planning question to the SMS.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the evidence that people intend to come, the real options, and the message the question would ride on, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what shows that people intend to come and are not stopped by cost, access, or trust.
Asks for the dates, hours, and places of the camp, or whether it happens once.
Asks which message the question would be added to or who sends it.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: At our four antenatal clinics in Malawi, women who test HIV-positive are counseled to tell their partner. Counselors say most women agree they should, but at the next visit few have. We want a card where the woman writes when and where she will tell him, filled in with the counselor at the end of the session. She can tell him any day before her next visit, four weeks later. Draft the prompt.
evals.expected_output: The skill drafts no more than a working copy and says a clinician or safeguarding lead must review who sees the plan and what support follows before any use.
assertions: Names a clinician or safeguarding lead who must review it before any use.
Says a written card naming when and where she will tell her partner could expose her, or asks who would see it.
Says the counselors' impression that women agree is weak evidence that they intend to tell their partner.
Says what to bring to the specialist.
Does not present a prompt as ready to print or use.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Our TB patients forget their daily pills. We want the clinic to text each patient every evening. How many messages should we send, at what time, and for how long?
evals.expected_output: The skill says this is a schedule of messages the program sends, not a plan the patient states, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says a message the program sends is different from a plan the person states.
